chapter: Rhythm and blues, the Howard Theatre and later years
title: House band at the Howard Theatre, 1951-54
summary: The Howard house band directed by Frank Wess included the Pogue brothers and Buck Hill, a Dunbar student then who, like others, admired Prez.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it

blocks.x: What happened then? From '51 to '53 you were at the Howard Theatre, right?
In between that time is when you went out with Bradshaw.
What kind of people came in to the Howard then, that you played with?

Oh yeah. Let's see. Frank Wess was directing the band. We had Julius Pogue, Pete Pogue, Fathead Pogue -- they was brothers; all of them played saxophone. And they had Wallace Cryer playing baritone. Buck Hill...
When did you first run into Buck Hill?
Oh man, I run into Buck Hill back there in '44 or '43 or something. He was going to school down at
Dunbar. He wasn't playing. He was just starting out then. He was playing pretty good, you know.
Who was he into? Did he have any favorites?
Well, most of those cats was Les, in them days -- Prez. Everybody was diggin' Prez in them days.
